newsitem.title: CHINA: China to send team to check U.S. farm products.
newsitem.headline: China to send team to check U.S. farm products.

text.p: China plans to send a scientific team to the United States to look at agricultural products amid phyto-sanitary concerns, California governor Pete Wilson said on Tuesday.
Wilson said he had discussed U.S. farm exports to China with officials during his current visit to China.
China would send a team of scientists to the U.S. in March, he said.
"There has evidently been an expression of some concern about violating phyto-sanitary standards," he told reporters.

"We are eager to have them come to California to ask any questions and to see whatever they want to see because I think we can make the case very effectively that they needn't be concerned about California exports," he said.
China was particularly concerned about medfly, he said.

California had very effectively dealt with medfly and imposed much tougher standards on its agriculture products, he said, adding that California's main exports included apples, plums and citrus fruits.
Medfly infestation can cause damage to yields in some 250 types of fruits, vegetables and other plants.
